query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a controlled amount of lattice distortion through cryogenic rolling can improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys by enhancing grain boundary cohesion and promoting dislocation-mediated plasticity.
generation.material_initial_state: Dual-phase lamellar colonies in eutectic high-entropy alloys
generation.intervention: Cryogenic rolling with a reduction ratio of 50% at a temperature of 77 K
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary cohesion and dislocation density
generation.mechanism: Enhanced grain boundary cohesion and dislocation-mediated plasticity due to lattice distortion introduced by cryogenic rolling
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in yield strength and 30% increase in tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline
generation.boundary: Applicable to eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies, processed through conventional casting and heat treatment methods
generation.uncertainty: The optimal reduction ratio and cryogenic temperature for maximizing strength and ductility may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and microstructure

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of cryogenically rolled and unmodified eutectic high-entropy alloy samples at room temperature
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength and tensile ductility of the cryogenically rolled sample are not significantly higher than the unmodified sample (i.e., less than 10% increase in yield strength and less than 15% increase in tensile ductility), the hypothesis is falsified
